ria: quick callout from today’s int6 bringup. tempesta-v2-int6 failing our tiny multiorient smoke with two consistent issues: (1) CJK vertical punctuation (brackets/quotes) glued to ideographs causing column reflow, (2) RTL bracket/paren visual mirroring flips in Hebrew/Arabic. repro below. :mag:
sam: can you paste the exact eval command and the smallest failing snippet?
tomo: running: `rrun eval --model=tempesta-v2-int6 --suite=multiorient_subtitles --subset=zh_vertical,hebrew_rtl,ar_math --shards=quick --jobs=6 --log-token-ids --log-detok`

ria: quick summary (quick shard):
``
zh_vertical: BLEU baseline=30.7 -> int6=24.3 (regressions 88/300)
hebrew_rtl: bracket_mirror errs baseline=0 -> int6=20/300
ar_math: brace-mirror/spacing baseline=0 -> int6=12/300
```

ria: minimal zh example: input line: "\uff08\u5317\u4eac\uff09\n"
baseline detok tokens: ["\uff08","\u5317\u4eac","\uff09"]
int6 detok tokens:   ["\uff08\u5317\u4eac\uff09"]  # opening bracket glued to ideograph -> column shift

ria: hebrew example: input: "\u05d0\u05e9\u05e8 (\u05e2\u05d1)"
baseline decode: "\u05d0\u05e9\u05e8 (\u05e2\u05d1)"
int6 decode:     "\u05d0\u05e9\u05e8 )\u05e2\u05d1("  # parentheses visually swapped in RTL render

claire: do token ids change? tokenizer changes would show id diffs.
ria: token ids are identical on the failing examples. I added `--log-token-ids` and saw identical sequences for compaction on/off. sample: `ids=[512,2048,77]` both runs, but detok differs.
zhen: packaging diffs for int6: per-head quant-scale folding, aggressive kvcache compaction heuristic, and packed-attn-quant kernel. no tokenizer edits. my hypothesis: compaction causes small hidden-state/attention shifts which cascade into detok/bidi shaping.
sam: try A/B: `--no-kvcache-compaction --force-stable-quant` and compare.
tomo: ran A/B on a 200-sample quick run: compaction off + stable-quant reduces zh regressions to 7/200 and hebrew flips to 0/200. compaction on alone reduces slightly. so compaction+quant fold interaction looks implicated.

claire: identical ids + different rendering implies downstream shaping or ZWJ/ZWSP insertion differences; maybe detok inserts an invisible marker when hidden-state crosses a threshold. can we diff per-token hidden-state L2 and attention mass?
zhen: I ran a micro hidden-state diff for an affected Hebrew prefix. per-token L2 deltas are ~1e-3 but attention mass on the bracket token shifts ~10-14% when compaction runs early. that correlates with the visual flip.

ria: sample logs attached (short):
``
# compaction ON (fail)
ids: [512,2048,77,99]
detok: "... )\u05e2\u05d1("
# compaction OFF (pass)
ids: [512,2048,77,99]
detok: "... (\u05e2\u05d1)"
# note: ids equal but final rendered order differs in RTL contexts
```

sam: can you push a tiny failing file to evals and a render? we'll want UX to see it.
omo: pushed `/evals/smoke/multiorient/repro_1911111111.txt` and renders at `/evals/smoke/renders/1911111111/` for screenshots.

claire: next action plan: 1) add a small multiorient smoke to the onboard CI that checks zh_vertical punctuation separation + hebrew/ar bracket orientation (50-sample shard), 2) gate aggressive kvcache compaction behind a mixed-orient request heuristic so we fall back to safe compaction for these sequences, 3) introduce `--quant-stability-mode` build flag to disable per-head folding for early canaries, 4) run a kernel-only revert (packed-attn-quant -> packed-attn) to confirm kernel interaction.
zhen: I ran a kernel revert locally: packed-attn (non-quant kernel) + compaction does not reproduce; packed-attn-quant + compaction does. opening bisect ticket BR-2045 with logs and the micro hidden-state diffs.

sam: good. let's land the CI smoke first so future builds are caught early. who wants to pair on the hidden-state diff harness? (it)s useful to compute per-token attention mass delta and ZWJ insertion diffs.
claire: I can pair tomorrow with zhen. I'll PR the smoke test this afternoon.
ci-bot: canary run queued: tempesta-int6-multiorient-canary #94021 (compaction=false)

ria: thanks team. I'll update BR-2045 with the repro links and attach the render PNGs for docs/UX. will also add a short note to the runbook about `--quant-stability-mode`. :memo:
